page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7se.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance from the Enhanced family built on KVM hypervisor virtualization. Powered by a 2.9 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor, this x86_64 instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU feature set includes instruction extensions such as AVX-512 VNNI, AES-NI, and VAES, backed by a 48 MB L3 cache array. It is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance provides a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and contains no attached local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluation highlights strong performance in specific memory-intensive and small-model inference tasks. The instance achieved a PassMark memory score of 2789.6, placing it in the top 25% tier, supported by uncached memory read bandwidth of 155.72 GB/sec and write throughput of 70.15 GB/sec. Small LLM inference text generation using a 135M parameter model reached 316.66 tokens/sec, also ranking in the top 25%. Compute-focused testing showed solid mid-range performance, with multi-core stress-ng scores reaching 31109.01 and PassMark CPU scoring at 36838.07. Redis SET throughput registered at 31.36 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput reached 33.55 GB/sec.

From a resource density and cost efficiency perspective, the instance maximizes CPU core allocation relative to system memory, offering balanced compute throughput for CPU-bound tasks. The lack of bundled local NVMe storage requires attachment to external cloud storage for persistent data requirements. Overall, the hardware profile and benchmark characteristics make the ecs.c7se.8xlarge well suited for compute-intensive workloads, static web serving, software compilation tasks, CPU-based small LLM inference, and in-memory key-value caching.

In synthetic testing, it demonstrates strong memory performance with a PassMark memory score of 2789.6 and efficient 135M LLM text generation at 316.66 tokens per second, alongside consistent middle-tier multi-core CPU throughput. Providing 2.0 GB of memory per vCPU, this instance offers a compute-dense execution profile suitable for software compilation, web serving, distributed key-value data stores, and CPU-driven machine learning workloads.
